To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the basis of the least dissipative Fourier modes can be used as a basis for the numerical simulation of low-Rm magnetized turbulence.

(1) the least dissipative mode approach can be used to study both two- and (weakly) three-dimensional low-Rms magnetohydrodynamic turbulent flows; (2) the least dissipating modes give a relevant prediction for a key quantity in two-dimensional flows (the scale of the first 3D structure to appear); (3) the least dissipate modes give an accurate prediction for the smallest scale in forced flows, as well as the scale separation in the three-dimensional flow;

the least dissipating modes can be used as a relevant basis to simulate low-Rm Mhd flows, and that the scaling of the smallest scales in the flow can be derived from a single parameter, the largest linear decay rate of the flow.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the dissipation operator is the key to the scaling of the smallest scales in MHD turbulence.
, in the low-Rm limit, the least dissipative eigenmodes of the MHD dissipation operator can be used as the basis functions for the numerical simulation of MHD turbulence in a periodic domain.

the use of the least dissipative basis is a very efficient way to perform direct numerical simulations of MHD turbulence at low-Rm, as it allows us to reduce the number of degrees of freedom of the problem, and therefore the computational cost, without any significant loss in accuracy.
